description: E-commerce demo site for automation practice. Full flow: login, browse/sort products, product detail, cart, three-step checkout, and a shared side (burger) menu available after login.

_inventory_conventions.components: Each page is tagged with the Jira Component(s) it belongs to (Login, Inventory, Cart, Checkout). Backlog 2.2 uses these to inject only the story-relevant pages into Agent 2's prompt. A page with "always": true is injected on every call regardless of component (the shared menu), analogous to app_context core.md. A story with no components — or a component that matches no page — safely gets ALL pages.
_inventory_conventions.selector_source: All selectors use SauceDemo's data-test attributes, which are stable and always present.
_inventory_conventions.errors: Prefer per-page `errors` (name -> exact message string, verbatim) over a big top-level `common_errors`. Page-level errors get filtered with their page by backlog 2.2, and keep messages next to the screen that raises them. Reserve top-level `common_errors` for truly global errors (e.g. a session-timeout banner).

test_users._note: Roles only — credentials are NEVER stored here. This file is sent to the LLM verbatim. Features log in by ROLE; the `credentials` fixture in tests/step_defs/conftest.py resolves the role from environment variables (APP_USER_<ROLE> / APP_PASSWORD). Use the role name in Gherkin, e.g. When I log in as "standard".
test_users.locked_out: receives a lockout error on login
test_users.problem: UI bugs intentionally present (broken images, form fields)

elements_notes.error_message_vs_close_button: IMPORTANT: [data-test='error'] is the <h3> element that holds the error text. The close (X) button is a SIBLING element, not a child. Do NOT write [data-test='error'] button or .locator('button') under the error message — that will not find anything. Use [data-test='error-button'] directly.

errors.invalid_credentials: Epic sadface: Username and password do not match any user in this service
errors.locked_out: Epic sadface: Sorry, this user has been locked out.

elements_notes.add_remove_button_ids: Each product's add/remove button has a slug suffix, e.g. [data-test='add-to-cart-sauce-labs-backpack'] then it flips to [data-test='remove-sauce-labs-backpack']. Use the ^= prefix selectors for 'any product', or the exact slug for a specific one.
elements_notes.sort_values: sort_dropdown is a native <select>. Option values: 'az' (Name A-Z), 'za' (Name Z-A), 'lohi' (Price low-high), 'hilo' (Price high-low). Use select_option(value=...).

elements_notes.continue_is_input: The Continue control is an <input type='submit'>, so [data-test='continue'] targets an input, not a <button>. Click it directly by the data-test.

checkout_step_one.implementation_status: NOT YET CREATED — customer-information form (step one of three)

elements_notes.totals_text: subtotal/tax/total labels contain the money as text, e.g. 'Item total: $29.99', 'Tax: $2.40', 'Total: $32.39'. Assert on the numeric substring, not exact full-string equality, since values vary with cart contents.

checkout_step_two.implementation_status: NOT YET CREATED — order overview / totals (step two of three)

elements_notes.success_text: complete_header reads 'Thank you for your order!' on a successful checkout. This is the canonical assertion for a completed purchase.

checkout_complete.implementation_status: NOT YET CREATED — order confirmation (step three of three)

menu.url: (overlay — available on every page after login)

elements_notes.shared_menu: This burger menu overlays every authenticated page (inventory, cart, checkout). It is tagged "always": true so it is injected on every Agent 2 call regardless of the story's component filter. The open/close buttons use id selectors (React Burger Menu component), which is the one place ids are acceptable on SauceDemo — the data-test attributes only appear on the links inside.
elements_notes.logout_returns_to_login: logout_link navigates back to '/' (the login page).

common_errors._note: Page-specific errors now live under each page's `errors` field so they ride the 2.2 component filter (a Login story injects only login errors). Put ONLY genuinely cross-cutting/global errors here.

avoid: IDs (some are generated; only the burger open/close buttons legitimately use ids)
